Title: Pela primeira vez em 2025, Fed reduz taxas de juros para faixa de 4% a 4,25% ao ano nos Estados Unidos

Summary: 
The Federal Reserve (Fed) lowered the United States federal funds rate on Wednesday, September 17, 2025, to a range of 4%–4.25% from the previous 4.25%–4.50%, marking the first cut of 2025. The committee plans two additional cuts this year. The new Fed governor, Stephen Miran, who was appointed by former President Donald Trump, voted against the decision and pushed for a larger cut, citing Trump’s pressure to reduce rates. The Fed’s monetary policy committee also expressed greater optimism about U.S. economic growth, projecting a 1.6% expansion for 2025, up from the 1.4% forecast in June, while keeping its unemployment and inflation outlook unchanged. The decision follows months of intense political pressure from Trump, who has since abandoned threats to remove Fed Chair Jerome Powell but is now seeking to dismiss FOMC member Lisa Cook over alleged mortgage‑fraud claims. 'Stephen Miran' voted against the rate cut, 'Jerome Powell' remains in office, and 'Lisa Cook' faces a potential dismissal.

Title: US-Fed: Kommt die Leitzinssenkung?

Summary: 
The U.S. Federal Reserve is poised to decide whether to cut the federal‑funds rate for the first time since December 2024 amid a weak labor market and inflation concerns.  Since December 2024 the Fed has kept the policy rate in a 4.25 %–4.5 % band, the level at which commercial banks borrow from the central bank.  Recent labor‑market data show that employment growth for the 12 months to March 2025 was revised down by 911,000 jobs, a large negative revision that signals slower economic expansion.  Analysts expect a 0.25‑point cut; the International Monetary Fund’s communications director Julie Kozack said the Fed could begin to trim the range cautiously.  Fed Chair Jerome Powell has advocated a lower rate to make mortgages cheaper and reduce debt‑service costs, while President Donald Trump has been pushing for cuts and has tried to pressure Powell and board member Lisa Cook, even threatening to fire Powell.  Trump’s tariff policy has also been cited as a factor that keeps businesses uncertain about investment, which in turn affects the labor market.  Economists Dirk Schumacher of KfW and Felix Schmidt of Berenberg both predict a cut, with Schumacher calling it "eine ausgemachte Sache" and Schmidt noting that "bevor der anhaltende Inflationsdruck weiteren Zinssenkungen dann einen Riegel vorschieben wird".  The article discusses the potential inflationary risks of a lower rate, noting that lower rates could fuel inflation, especially given recent U.S. import tariffs.

Published date: September 17 2025, 05:57

URL: https://www.finanzen.net/nachricht/zinsen/schwacher-us-arbeitsmarkt-experten-erwarten-leitzinssenkung-durch-die-us-notenbank-fed-14839525

Title: Fed’s Official Backs Three Rate Cuts In 2025 As Labour Market Weakens

Bowman dissented at the last Fed meeting, favouring an immediate cut to pre-empt further economic weakness. The Fed has three remaining meetings this year, leaving scope for the cuts Bowman envisions.

Title: Fed Delivers First Rate Cut of 2025

Summary: 
The Federal Reserve trimmed its key interest rate by a quarter‑point to a 4%–4.25% range, marking the first cut of 2025.  The Fed signaled that two additional cuts are expected this year.  Earlier meetings had kept the rate unchanged amid a softening job market and concerns that President Trump’s tariffs could spur inflation, according to the AP.  Fed Chair Jerome Powell’s 2:30 p.m. Eastern time news conference will be closely watched for his assessment of the economy and the likelihood of further cuts next year.
